CSS 551 · Advanced 3D Computer Graphics

HW4 · Viewing and rasterization

Out Thursday October 29 · due Wednesday November 4, 11:59 PM on Canvas · 2.5 % of the course grade · Unity or WebGL · hub · schedule · syllabus · all homework
Read before this homework: Viewing §2, the view matrix · §5, the projection matrix · §8, the full chain · Rasterization §1, edge functions · §4, barycentric coordinates · Unity Shaders §4

What you build

The two matrices that turn a placed world into pixels, checked entry by entry against the text's numbers, then the whole chain for one vertex: model, view, projection, the divide, the viewport. Then the other half of the pipeline: which pixels a triangle covers, by three edge functions per pixel center. The runner renders the scene through your V and P (three.js is told not to compute its own) and marks where your chain puts the cube's corner.

JavaScriptC#What it computes
viewMatrixViewMatrixV with rows u, v, w and column 3 = −(u·eye, v·eye, w·eye); w = normalize(eye − at), u = normalize(up × w), v = w × u.
perspectiveMatrixPerspectiveMatrixThe OpenGL perspective matrix: f = 1 / tan(fovY/2); row 3 = (0, 0, −1, 0).
worldToPixelWorldToPixel(pixel x, pixel y, NDC depth) of an object point through M, V, P, the divide and the viewport; pixel y counts DOWN from the top-left.
edgeEdgeTwice the signed area of (a, b, p).
barycentricBarycentricThe three weights of p in the triangle, each an edge function over the triangle's own.
rasterizeRasterizeThe pixels (i, j) of a res × res grid over [0, 1]² whose center ((i + ½)/res, (j + ½)/res) has all three weights ≥ 0.
  • The camera looks down −w; NDC depth runs from −1 at the near plane to 1 at the far plane (OpenGL).
  • The model matrix of the checks is given: T(0, 0.5, 0) · Ry(30).
  • Use the triangle's vertices exactly as listed below (six decimals): rounded to three, one pixel center at 12 × 12 changes sides.

Implement and replace

Build each function from primitives (dot, cross, normalize, matrix products, applying a matrix to a point, tan.) and use the engine's own helper, where one exists, only to check your result. These are off limits in your submission:

TrackOff limits
WebGL (JavaScript)lookAtBasis and perspective from xform.js; THREE.Matrix4.lookAt, makePerspective; camera.updateProjectionMatrix; Vector3.project.
Unity (C#)Matrix4x4.LookAt, Perspective, TRS, .inverse; Camera.worldToCameraMatrix, projectionMatrix, WorldToScreenPoint; GL.GetGPUProjectionMatrix.

Getting started

WebGL track.
  1. Download the course site: its repository (Code, then Download ZIP), or git clone it.
  2. From the site's root folder run python3 -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000/homework/run.html?hw=hw04.
  3. Edit lib/skeletons/hw04.js, the only file you change, and reload: the Checks table under the scene compares your numbers with the ones below.

The unfilled skeleton runs on this site too, so you can see the page before you start.

Unity track.
  1. In Unity Hub, create a new project with the 3D (Built-In Render Pipeline) template in editor 6000.3.11f1.
  2. From the same download, copy the files in homework/hw04/unity/ into Assets/HW04/.
  3. Create an empty GameObject, add the Checks component (namespace CSS551.HW04), and press Play: the Console lists every check with your value and the expected one.
  4. Edit HW04.cs; the other files are given.

The Unity files compile against a stand-in for the UnityEngine API and pass their checks with the reference solution, but they are new this quarter and have not yet been opened in the Unity editor. If one does not compile in 6000.3.11f1, post the error on the Canvas board and use the WebGL track meanwhile.

Submitting and grading

  • WebGL: the one file hw04.js.
  • Unity: the project folder, zipped, without Library/, Temp/, Logs/ and obj/.

Grading runs your functions twice: on the published inputs above and on a second set of inputs that is not published. A check earns its points only when your value is within its tolerance on both, so the numbers have to come from the math. The score is the sum of the points earned, out of 100. A submission that does not load or compile earns no check points. Name any collaborators and tools in the submission comment.

Late tokens. You have two for the quarter. Declare one in the submission comment to extend this homework by 24 hours without penalty. Beyond tokens, late homework loses 10 % per day for up to three days.
